implementationPlan.description:
The atomic three-part move — DoD 0's write half, in ONE command decision.
THREE THINGS MOVE TOGETHER OR NOTHING DOES: the predecessor is marked SUPERSEDED; the successor becomes ACTIVE at PREDECESSOR EPOCH + 1; and the PAIRED preparation records are marked CONSUMED. Rail 2 forbids a compensating second commit, and the failure mode is unrecoverable rather than merely untidy — a superseded predecessor with no active successor leaves the project with NO CURRENT GRAPH, and nothing can compensate that afterwards.
EPOCH + 1 IS RELATIVE TO THE PREDECESSOR. Not a global counter, not an assumption of epoch 1. An implementation that increments a counter or hard-codes 1 passes the first supersession and corrupts the second — assert the arithmetic against the predecessor's own epoch.
ONE ACTIVE REVISION AT A TIME is a write-side guard, not a read-side convention. Enforce it where the write happens, and drill it under interleaving rather than sequentially.
Use the landed multi-leg decision seam so all three legs ride one decision. Fence with `store.getAggregateVersion` and read back through STORE EVENTS — a secondary leg's aggregate never enters `DurableLedger.aggregates`, so `versionOf(ledger, ...)` reads 0 after a perfectly successful commit and a ledger-based verifier would refuse every honest supersession.
implementationPlan.note:
WRITE HALF LANDED — SIX legs, ONE commitAcceptedLegs. legs[0] is the GOAL (goal.advance_graph_epoch), then predecessor graph.supersede, successor whole-history graph.approve, and the three preparation-pair consumption legs. graph-supersede-legs.ts + graph-supersede-consumption.ts + graph-supersede-service.ts.

EPOCH+1 IS RELATIVE TO THE PREDECESSOR and asserted twice against two independent durable facts: buildSupersessionRevisionLegs computes predecessor.graphEpoch + 1 off the REPLAYED predecessor state, and goal.advance_graph_epoch independently requires graphEpoch === nextGraphEpoch(goalState) AND predecessorGraphRevisionRef === goal.activeGraphRevisionRef. A private counter or a hard-coded 1 cannot satisfy both.

ONE ACTIVE IS A WRITE-SIDE GUARD: the successor aggregate must have ZERO events (graph-supersede-facts.ts), the predecessor must BE the durable ACTIVE revision, and the successor leg fences at expectedVersion 0 while the predecessor leg fences at store.getAggregateVersion. Secondary-leg versions come from store.getAggregateVersion, never versionOf(ledger, ...) — the ledger folds only the primary target.

CONSUMPTION IS NOT RELEASE: consumeGeneration keeps refunded at 0 and both members land CONSUMED; PREPARATION_TERMINAL_EVENT_TYPES makes foldPreparationHistory treat both terminals alike, so a post-consumption releasePreparation answers SUPERSESSION_RELEASE_GENERATION_ABSENT (asserted).

DELETED AN UNFALSIFIABLE GUARD: GRAPH_SUPERSEDE_PREPARATION_NOT_HELD. foldPreparationHistory returns `current` only for a PREPARED record (funding HELD, fence ACTIVE by construction) and both terminals clear it, so the check was answered earlier on every path — deleting it left every arm green. Roster is now 15 codes.

ACCEPTED CONTROL GREEN, built entirely through production writers (activateApprovedGraph -> commitPreparation -> putGraphBody): epoch 1 -> 2, predecessor SUPERSEDED, successor ACTIVE with node-b, pair CONSUMED, 9 new arms executed. `npx vitest run src/planning/graph-supersede-service.test.ts` -> Test Files 1 passed (1) / Tests 51 passed (51). implementationPlan.description:
The request fence and the refusal roster — DoD 1 and DoD 2.
DoD 1 — THE REQUEST MAY IDENTIFY THE TARGET AND NOTHING MORE. It cannot supply active projection, epoch, lifecycle, funding, disposition, carry authority, content bytes outside the SEALED proposal, or an already-ACTIVE state. Eight categories; refuse each STRUCTURALLY at the payload allow-list rather than defending against it downstream. Every missing or unverifiable fact refuses with an exact service/upstream code and layer and ZERO events.
DoD 2 — FIVE REFUSAL CLASSES, each pinned with exact code, layer AND REFUSING AGGREGATE: wrong predecessor/successor; preparation DRIFT; stale version/epoch; changed bytes under one decision identity; concurrent activation.
THE CRITICAL PROPERTY ON EVERY ONE: THEY REFUSE **WITHOUT CONSUMING PREPARATION OR ADVANCING AN EPOCH**. Assert BOTH absences on each arm. A refusal that consumed the preparation has destroyed the very thing a retry needs, and one that advanced an epoch has moved the graph without replacing it — both are worse than the original failure.
SAME-BYTE REPLAY returns the ORIGINAL IMMUTABLE RECORD with unchanged event and decision counts. Assert the counts, not just the returned value.
implementationPlan.note:
REFUSAL ROSTER LANDED — graph-supersede-refusals.test.ts, 68 executed arms (Test Files 1 passed / Tests 68 passed).

DoD 1 — STRUCTURAL, at the payload allow-list. GRAPH_SUPERSEDE_REQUEST_KEYS is an EXACT 11-key set; GRAPH_SUPERSEDE_FORBIDDEN_KEYS names DoD 1's eight categories (activation, carryAuthority, dispositions, funding, graphContentBytes, graphEpoch, lifecycle, planningDisposition) and it.each sweeps all eight -> GRAPH_SUPERSEDE_REQUEST_INVALID / GRAPH_SUPERSEDE_SERVICE / layer GRAPH_SUPERSEDE. Denominators pinned EXACTLY (15 codes, 4 authorities, 11 request keys, 8 forbidden keys) with a disjointness assertion so a forbidden key that was also accepted could not make its own arm unfalsifiable. Content bytes: the successor hash is a LOOKUP KEY and an unsealed one refuses with GRAPH_BODY_ABSENT / GRAPH_BODY_RECORD as source.

DoD 2 — every class pinned with code + refusedBy (+ source where a lower reader answered), and EVERY service-level arm runs through expectRefusedWithNoResidue, which re-reads the six aggregates' event counts, the still-current generation number and the live graph epoch and requires them unchanged, plus an unchanged readEventHorizon. That is DoD 2's "refuses WITHOUT consuming preparation or advancing an epoch", asserted as BOTH absences on every arm rather than argued.
Arms: WRONG PREDECESSOR x2 (foreign revision; goal that does not own the active graph), WRONG SUCCESSOR x2 (successor IS predecessor; successor aggregate already has a history — reached from the post-supersession world), CONTENT UNSEALED, PREPARATION ABSENT, NEAR-MISS GENERATION (generation+1), STALE VERSION (version+1), DRIFT x2 (goal epoch and goal active-revision disagreeing with the projection, through readSupersedeFacts' own production `goal` parameter), FUNDING_UNAVAILABLE (injected budget port), PREPARATION_UNVERIFIABLE (corrupt history -> PREPARATION_HISTORY_MALFORMED / SUPERSESSION_PREPARATION_HISTORY), GOAL_UNREADABLE, TARGET_FOREIGN, CURRENT_GRAPH_UNAVAILABLE (ACTIVE_GRAPH_ABSENT / ACTIVE_GRAPH_PROJECTION), BYTES_CONFLICT, plus same-byte replay with unchanged event and decision COUNTS.

TWO DISCLOSED UNTESTED PATHS, both named rather than hidden: (1) GRAPH_SUPERSEDE_CONCURRENT_ACTIVATION is the store's own expected-version fence and is unreachable from a single-process fixture because the read-side predecessor check answers first — the concurrent arm therefore pins GRAPH_SUPERSEDE_PREDECESSOR_MISMATCH, which is the honest code. (2) The preparation-side drift conditions (targetRevisionRef / captured epoch / lineages / dispositionDigest) have no reachable arm because the only mutation that could move them is a second preparation generation, which is blocked — see the finding below.

MEASURED FINDING, PINNED BY ITS OWN ARM: a committed supersession makes the goal's budget projection unreadable. Every budget-ledger record carries the graphRevisionRef/graphEpoch it was authorized at and budget-current-projection.ts:113 refuses BUDGET_PROJECTION_STALE_BINDING when they disagree with the current binding, which the supersession just advanced. Nothing re-authorizes a budget root at a new epoch, so proposeSupersessionPreparation then answers SUPERSESSION_PREPARATION_BUDGET_UNAVAILABLE and no second supersession is reachable. Not introduced by this row and not owned by it; pinned so the day budget re-authorization lands the arm goes red.

FOREIGN RED DISCLOSED: `npx tsc --project tsconfig.json` now reports src/planning/node-mission-producer.ts(245,19) TS2345 NODE_MISSION_WORKSPACE_DISAGREEMENT. That file is UNTRACKED (`git status --porcelain` -> `??`), contains zero references to this task, and was clean at my earlier typecheck in this same session — a peer's in-flight file. Real SqliteEventStore tests and mutation drills — DoD 3.
THE ACCEPTED CONTROL IS BUILT THROUGH PRODUCTION WRITERS: the parent's approve leg (task-eacea969) for the predecessor and successor revisions, and task-32c1ba45's preparation writers for the generation. A hand-seeded pair is the mock-backed accepted path rail 2 refuses — and it is especially tempting here, because seeding two graph revisions and a preparation record is easy and looks convincing.
Assert NONZERO hostile and interleaving counts (a zero-case matrix passes while proving nothing) and ZERO PARTIAL RESIDUE at EVERY fault boundary — inject a failure at each of the three legs in turn and confirm nothing moved.
MUTATION DRILLS DoD 3 names, each run ALONE (a first red masks a second). Back up untracked paths by SHA256 outside the tree, restore proved in a SEPARATE call:
  (a) ONE-ACTIVE: allow the predecessor to stay ACTIVE alongside the successor — the one-active guard must red. Drill under interleaving, not sequentially.
  (b) EPOCH+1: activate at a fixed epoch or a global counter instead of predecessor + 1 — the epoch arm must red. Use a predecessor whose epoch is NOT 1, or the mutant passes.
  (c) PREPARATION CONSUMPTION: leave the paired preparations unconsumed — that arm must red.
  (d) CALLER-AUTHORITY: accept a caller-supplied current fact instead of the durable one — the DoD-1 arm must red. Run per category.
  (e) NEAR-MISS GENERATION: supersede against a generation differing only in version — the exactness arm must red. This is the drill for the row's title property.
  (f) REFUSAL RESIDUE: make a refusal path consume the preparation — the no-consumption arm must red.

planningNotes.risks:
1. EXACTNESS IS THE DELIVERABLE. A near-miss generation still commits and still tests green while superseding the wrong preparation. Assert the generation AND version by equality, and drill a near-miss explicitly.

2. THE THREE-PART MOVE IS ONE DECISION. Predecessor SUPERSEDED, successor ACTIVE at predecessor epoch + 1, paired preparations CONSUMED — together or not at all. Prove it with an injected failure showing zero rows moved, not by asserting atomicity in prose.

3. EPOCH + 1 IS RELATIVE TO THE PREDECESSOR, not to a counter and not to 1. An implementation that increments a global or assumes epoch 1 passes the first test and corrupts the second supersession.

4. A POSITIVE CONTROL MUST USE A SYMBOL THAT EXISTS. I nearly filed a false absence by using the two MISSING symbols as their own control. Use `releaseWork` or similar against packages/scheduler/src to prove the grep shape before trusting any empty result.

5. THE ACCEPTED CONTROL MUST BE BUILT THROUGH PRODUCTION WRITERS (DoD 3): the parent's approve leg AND 32c1ba45's preparation writers. A hand-seeded predecessor/successor pair is the mock-backed accepted path rail 2 refuses — and it is especially tempting here because seeding two graph revisions is easy.

6. REFUSALS MUST NOT CONSUME PREPARATION OR ADVANCE AN EPOCH (DoD 2). Assert BOTH absences on every refusal arm — a refusal that consumed the preparation has destroyed the thing a retry needs.

7. RECOMPUTE THE FULL CONTENT HASH via `encodeGraphContent`; never equate snapshotIdentity/graphIdentity with graphContentHash (rail 1).

8. DO NOT REGISTER `graph.supersede` — task-931f99e8 owns it and a duplicate crashes daemon composition.
